snapshots.priorP01HistoricalConflict: Installer reserved by G1-A / forbidden to G1-B

observedProblem: Malformed WebMessage JSON with a valid requestId already reserved by an in-flight or completed native action could fail validation on kind or routeId before duplicate detection, leading to a second REJECTED/P01_BAD_MESSAGE reply while the first native action could later COMPLETED. This is a source-code defect; no runtime exploit observed.
actualFix: Extract requestId independently for JSON objects before other-field validation; if it matches the established request-ID grammar and is in the document replay set, silently ignore duplicate even when kind/route is malformed. Leave new malformed request IDs on existing P01_BAD_MESSAGE path, keep eight-inflight and 1024-document ceilings, native consent, HOME/MENU/CORE, HTTPS-origin, popup suppression and ProcessFailed intact. No new WPF host.

blocker.ownerRequest: C08 original WPF-host owner should wire exactly this adapter to its existing single WebView2 host and independently test malformed duplicate requestId before/during/after native callback, HOME/MENU/CORE, permitted routes, consent, errors, origin, window.open and navigation on Windows. lesson.applied: R08 proved popup navigation has a separate WebView2 event family and keeps a single existing host; R09 preserves all previously DONE native/origin gates and reviews reply behavior for malformed duplicate messages.
lesson.new: Deduplication must precede schema rejection whenever an incoming record contains an independently extractable, syntactically valid reserved requestId. Otherwise a malformed replay may generate an inconsistent second rejection for a native action still in flight. A source-level PASS is not real runtime proof.
